getFocusPatterns.title: Explore your focus patterns
getFocusPatterns.what: Calculates uninterrupted work lengths and focus-review scores by type and activity by local hour. Includes sample sizes and whether evidence qualifies for recommendation personalization.
getFocusPatterns.why: Helps interpret habits together with their evidence. The same rules can inform later Chore recommendations when enough history exists.
steps: Validate the offset-aware from/to range and load history and timezone.
Consider completed sessions ending in the range and derive active intervals.
Group whole uninterrupted intervals of at least five minutes by type and split activity by local hour.
Calculate medians, quartiles, sample sizes and eligibility and return patterns.
notes: Type-duration quartiles describe the middle spread of uninterrupted blocks, not a productivity ranking. Hourly results use your saved local timezone.
The range includes start and excludes end; from must precede to. This does not edit preferences or plans.

Eligibility requires at least five qualifying intervals. With three or more focus reviews it requires five sessions and a median focus score of at least 3; with fewer reviews it requires eight sessions.

getAnalyticsSummary.why: Helps you review what actually happened rather than treating planned work as completed work. Missing evidence yields empty totals or unavailable statistics instead of invented scores.
steps: Validate offset-aware from and to with from earlier than to.
Load owned history, events, reviews, work context, types and preferences.
Derive event-based intervals, clip time to the requested range and calculate totals and medians.
Return the summary.
notes: The range includes its start and excludes its end. Historical session context is preferred, with current work as fallback.

Return database/migration status and expected/current revisions, or 503 for unavailable or outdated state.
notes: SELECT 1 reads no application table; django_migrations is Django framework migration history.
Public and read-only: does not create migration history, apply migrations, start the worker or verify email delivery.
No database writes are performed by this operation.

healthVersion.title: Read the running release identity
healthVersion.what: Returns package version and configured release SHA, branch and repository metadata. Does not read application data.
healthVersion.why: Identifies which release a responding server runs during deployment investigation. Version metadata does not establish database or worker readiness.
steps: Read installed package version and runtime build metadata.
Return the metadata with no-store caching.
notes: Public and read-only; no counters, audit events or application-row updates.
No database writes are performed by this operation.
